system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Backend Engineer | Python, Go & Distributed Systems
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 |
linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
PROFILE
Backend engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building large-scale backend
systems in Python, Go and C++. Designed and led services and platforms, including systems serving
50M+ users and an entitlement service handling 120k requests per second at peak. Hands-on engineer
who continues to code weekly, primarily on internal tooling in recent years.
CORE SKILLS
Backend development: Python, Go, C++, Django, Flask, FastAPI, Tornado, asyncio, REST APIs
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Pub/Sub
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP, GKE, BigQuery, AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes, Terraform
Reliability and engineering: Distributed systems design, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry,
architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH, Munich | 2019 - 2026 (Aug)
• Led the platform organisation of 5 teams, 45 engineers and 5 engineering managers, responsible for
identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
• Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE;
playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
• Reduced cloud spend by 31% (EUR 4.2M per year) through rightsizing, committed use discounts
and an internal cost dashboard.
• Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted
company-wide.
• Grew the organisation from 18 to 45 engineers and ran more than 200 interviews.
Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH | 2015 - 2019
• Served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, an internal FastAPI-like
framework, Cassandra and Redis.
• Designed a Go and Cassandra entitlement service handling 120k requests per second at peak.
• Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.
Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart | 2010 - 2015
• Built backend services for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++,
Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
• Led a team of 6 developers on the route-history product.
Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe | 2005 - 2010
• Developed C++ and Python for industrial data acquisition software on Linux and embedded x86.
• Built a Python test harness used by QA for 8 years.
EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc) in Computer Science | Rhine Valley University | 2005
LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)
SELECTED PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
• “Running Python at 100k rps” - EuroPython-style conference talk, 2018
• “Cost is a feature” - internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing &
Tracking team. My background combines hands-on Python and Go backend engineering with
experience building reliable, high-volume APIs and ingesting operational data—work that
maps closely to your event ingestion and live tracking platform.
At Streamhaus, I was technical lead for the playback API and designed a Go and Cassandra
entitlement service that handled 120k requests per second at peak. Later, as Director of
Engineering, Platform, I led the migration from a Python 2 monolith to around 60 Python
and Go services on GKE, improving playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. I
continue to code weekly, primarily on internal tooling in recent years, and bring experience
with Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform and observability tools
including Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry.
Earlier, at Nordfels Telematik, I built backend services ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles
and worked with PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ. That experience gives me a direct
connection to the operational data flows behind shipment tracking. I have also introduced
architecture review and on-call practices, and co-authored service and Python engineering
guidance—experience relevant to dependable services, clear design notes and shared
production ownership.
Tessel’s focus on turning carrier events into a reliable live picture of shipments is a strong
match for the systems I have built. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
backend and platform experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.
Sincerely,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
